name: Your app on OCI
summary: Attach an HTTPS Container Instances target to an existing app, preserving its source, database, storage and identity provider.

runtime.name: Existing Linux amd64 container
runtime.requirement: Stateless HTTP service with tested external persistence and background work absent or disabled

tools.name: terraform
tools.requirement: >= 1.7; backend operations may require a newer tested version
tools.purpose: Validate reviewed infrastructure and run mocked provider contract tests

application_contract.image: Private OCIR Linux amd64 image pinned by sha256, with no secrets baked into image layers.
application_contract.port: Configurable unprivileged port; the app must listen on 0.0.0.0 and honor its declared port.
application_contract.health: Configurable unauthenticated non-sensitive HTTP path returning 200 when ready; HTTPS is terminated at the load balancer.
application_contract.secrets: Only Vault identifiers enter Terraform and environment metadata. Application code must implement and test resource-principal retrieval.
application_contract.external_dependencies: Retain database, storage and authentication. Verify TLS, callbacks, egress, persistence, latency and rollback before accepting hosting.
application_contract.background_work: Target jobs must be absent or disabled by actual app controls with reviewed evidence. This target never transfers scheduler ownership.

operating_modes.description: Separate target and state, restricted HTTPS client ranges, source hosting retained and background workers disabled.
Explicit separate target after tested image promotion, user workflows and recovery. Traffic changes require their own approved operation.

acceptance.description: The existing app passes its own tests and container checks; source is preserved and the exact digest is recorded.
Session, target, subnet security lists, routes, certificate, image pull and selected secret access are reviewed; denied reads remain unknown.
Source and OCI pass meaningful browser workflows, identity and two-user checks, persistence, dependency TLS and bounded latency checks.
Isolated restore and image/traffic rollback are tested, with one scheduler owner and retained billable resources recorded.
